═══ THE DIAGNOSTIC RUN THE FIRST [operator-attested] CRITERION ASKS FOR — it WAS obtainable after
all, and here is the before/after pair on the same gate, same config, same commit. ═══

I previously recorded that this criterion "did not happen and now cannot" because the seam had been
named by a local experiment and the code was already fixed. **That was wrong, and the completion
verifier was right to fail the ticket for it.** The criterion asks for a run with STEP 0 PRESENT and
the WIRING FIX ABSENT — and that build is constructible from this very commit by reverting the single
`_effective_config` line, which is the same mutation the RED test uses. So I built it and ran it live.

**METHOD.** `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`: `cfg = _effective_config(self._config, req)` reverted to
`cfg = self._config`; Step 0's ContextVar + `step`/`model_class` recording left intact. Real
`rebar review-code --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD` (attested), `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` on, and a class table
whose values differ from `cfg.model` in BOTH model and provider:

    cfg.model = claude-opus-4-8                          (anthropic — the fall-through target)
    frontier  = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    standard  = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6

The mutation was applied by a script with a `trap ... EXIT` restore, and the worktree was verified
clean (`git diff --quiet src/rebar/llm/runner.py`) before anything else was allowed to run.

**BEFORE — pre-fix, 9 calls, EVERY ONE on `cfg.model` despite its declaration:**

    step      op                                            declared   ran
    ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    base      code-review-base                              frontier   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-docs                              frontier   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-tests                             frontier   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-deletion-impact                   frontier   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries    frontier   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    round_b   code-review-api-compat                        frontier   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    verify    code-review-verify                            standard   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    coach     code-review-coach                             standard   anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    (none)    code-novelty                                  (none)     anthropic:claude-opus-4-8

**AFTER — same gate, same class table, fix present:**

    base      code-review-base                              frontier   bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-docs / -tests / -deletion-impact /
              -project-review-phase-boundaries              frontier   bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    verify    code-review-verify                            standard   bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
    coach     code-review-coach                             standard   bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
    (none)    code-novelty                                  (none)     anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- sibling bug afeb

**WHAT THE PAIR ESTABLISHES that neither half could alone.** The `declared` column is identical in
both runs, so the declarations were always reaching the engine — Step 0 proves that independently of
the fix. What changes between the runs is ONLY the `ran` column. That isolates the defect to the step
BETWEEN "declaration resolved" and "model invoked", which is precisely
`PydanticAIRunner.run`'s `cfg = self._config`. This is the per-step attribution naming the broken
seam, which is what the criterion is for.

It also captures `round_b` (`code-review-api-compat`), which the post-fix Bedrock run did not exercise
because Round-B membership is escalation-driven — so the BEFORE table covers all five declaring steps.

**AND IT CONFIRMS THE DIAGNOSIS OF THE SIBLING.** `code-novelty` is `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` in
BOTH runs — unchanged by the fix, because it never had a declaration to honour. That is exactly the
signature of `afeb` (a hand-built sub-call inheriting raw `cfg`), and it is visibly a DIFFERENT defect
from the one fixed here: b690's fix moves every declaring step and leaves this one untouched.

**A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM ON THIS TICKET.** The comment asserting this criterion was
unsatisfiable stands superseded. The reasoning error was treating "the code is fixed" as making the
pre-fix state unreachable, when the pre-fix build is one line away and the ticket's own test suite
already relies on constructing it.
